Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 76, verses 1–2:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?﴾ ﴿Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixed, that We may test him; and We made him hearing and seeing.﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying ﴿Has there come upon man﴾: certainly there has come upon man. The word "hal" (has/whether) in this position is affirmative, not negative, as when one says to another, seeking to confirm: "Have I not honoured you?" when he has honoured him; or "Have I not visited you?" when he has visited him. It may be negative in other contexts, as when one says to another: "Does anyone do such a thing?" meaning: no one does that. The man of whom He, may His praise be exalted, speaks in this place, ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time from time﴾, is Adam ﷺ, so.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Has there come upon man﴾ — Adam — "there came upon him a period of time, he was not a thing worth mentioning." Man was created here only recently; what is known of God's creation was after man.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning﴾, he said: Adam ﷺ was the last of creation to be created.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time﴾, he said: Adam.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿a period of time﴾

The interpreters differed regarding the extent of this "period" (hin) mentioned by God in this place. Some of them said: it is forty years. They said: the clay of Adam remained shaped, without the spirit being breathed into it, for forty years; that is the extent of the period mentioned by God in this place. They said: that is why it was said: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning﴾, because there came upon him, while he was a shaped body into which the spirit had not been breathed, forty years, so he was a thing, but he was not a thing worth mentioning. They said: the meaning of His saying ﴿he was not a thing worth mentioning﴾ is that he was not a thing of distinction, nor of elevation, nor of honour; he was only clay that sticks and black mud moulded.

Others said: there is no limit to the "period" in this place. This view may be entered from the fact that God informed that there came upon man a period of time; and it is not understood in speech to say that there came upon man a period before he existed and before he was a thing. If that were intended, one would say "a period came before he was created," and not "came upon him." As for "time" (dahr) in this place, it has no limit at which one may stop.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixed, that We may test him﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We created the offspring of Adam from a sperm-drop, meaning: from the water of the man and the water of the woman. The "nutfah" (sperm-drop) is any small quantity of water in a container, whether it be a well or a waterskin or other, as 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah said:

"Are you not but a drop in a waterskin?" [Footnote: this is a rajaz verse in a long report, Al-Khizanah 3:17, said in mockery of a man whom they threw into a well and then made rajaz about him. The "mai'h" is the man who goes down to the bottom of the well when its water is scant, throws the buckets, fills them with his hand and bails for his companions.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿amshaj﴾

It means: mixtures. Its singular is "mashj" and "masheej," like "khidn" and "khadeen"; and from it is the saying of Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj:

"They cast down every hastened, gushing one... who was not clothed in skin in blood of mixtures." [Footnote: the first is without doubt the most correct of the sayings... (long discussion of the poem and of a ḥadīth)]

It is said from it: "I mashajtu this with this," when I mix it with it; and it is "mamshuj" with it and "masheej," i.e., mixed with it, as Abu Dhu'ayb said:

"As if the feather and the two ends of it, between the blade, were smeared with mashiij."

[Footnote on Ḥadīth 140: this is a fabricated ḥadīth with no basis... (the editor notes that Ibn Ḥibbān said of Ismā'īl ibn Yaḥyā ibn 'Abd Allāh al-Taymī that he was a liar; that the chain contains an unknown narrator; that 'Aṭiyyah ibn Sa'd al-'Awfī is weak; and the note on Zabrīq as the laqab of Ibrāhīm's father.)]

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of "amshaj" intended in this place. Some said: it is the mixing of the man's water with the woman's water.

Those who said that:

Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, both saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn al-Asbahani, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿amshajin nabtalihi﴾: "the water of the man and the water of the woman mix, one with the other."

Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn al-Asbahani, from Ikrimah, who said: the water of the man and the water of the woman mix together.

He said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: the water of the woman and the water of the man mix.

He said: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from al-Suddi, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: the water of the woman and the water of the man mix together.

He said: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: when the water of the man and the water of the woman gather, it is "amshaj."

He said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: al-Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: the water of the woman was mixed with the water of the man.

He said: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad informed us, from Mujahid, who said: God created the child from the water of the man and the water of the woman, and God has said: ﴿O mankind, indeed We created you from male and female﴾.

He said: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, who said: created from successive portions of the water of the man and the water of the woman.

Others said: what is meant is: Indeed We created man from a sperm-drop of various colours, through which he passes: it becomes a sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then bone, then it is clothed with flesh.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed We created man from a sperm-drop mixed, that We may test him﴾: "amshaj": created of colours; created from earth, then from the water of the womb and the uterus, which is the sperm-drop; then a clot; then a lump; then bone; then He brought him forth as another creation.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, regarding this verse, "amshaj": a sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump, then bone.

Al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir and Ya'qub al-Hadrami narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Simak, from Ikrimah, who said: a sperm-drop, then a clot.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed We created man from a sperm-drop mixed﴾: stages of creation, at one stage a sperm-drop, at another a clot, at another a lump, at another bones; then God clothed the bones with flesh, then brought him forth as another creation, causing hair to grow on him.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿amshajin nabtalihi﴾, he said: "amshaj": the water and blood mixed, then it was a clot, then it was a lump.

Others said: what is meant by this is the variation in the colours of the sperm-drop.

Those who said that:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿amshajin nabtalihi﴾: means: of differing colours.

Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: the colours of the sperm-drop.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: whichever of the two waters precedes, the child resembles its paternal and maternal uncles.

He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿amshajin nabtalihi﴾: the colours of the sperm-drop; the man's sperm-drop is white and red, and the woman's sperm-drop is red and green.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

Others said: rather, they are the veins that occur in the sperm-drop.

Those who said that:

Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham narrated to us, both saying: Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-Mas'udi narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mukhariq, from his father, from 'Abd Allah, who said: its "amshaj" are its veins.

Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Usamah ibn Zayd narrated to us, from his father, who said: they are the veins that occur in the sperm-drop.

The most likely of these sayings to be correct is the saying of him who said: the meaning of ﴿from a sperm-drop mixed﴾ is the sperm-drop of the man and the sperm-drop of the woman, because God described the sperm-drop as "amshaj," and when it has moved and become a clot, it has changed from the meaning of sperm-drop, so how can it be a mixed sperm-drop when it is a clot? As for those who said that the man's sperm-drop is white and red, what is known of the man's sperm-drop is that it is a single colour, white tending to red; and if it is one colour it is not various colours. I suppose that those who said "they are the veins in the sperm-drop" intended this meaning.

Ibn Humayd also narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: man was created only from a small quantity of sperm-drop. Do you not see that when a child is still, there appears to be like a trace of it? Indeed the son of Adam was created from such a thing, from the sperm-drop, mixed, that We may test him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that We may test him﴾

We try him. Some of the grammarians said: the meaning is: We made him hearing and seeing so that We may test him; this is an advanced form whose meaning is delayed, the meaning being: We created him and made him hearing and seeing so that We may test him. But what he said has no sound basis in my view, because testing is only with soundness of the faculties and the soundness of reason free from defects, even if hearing and sight are lacking. As for His informing us in this verse that He made for us hearing and sight, this is a reminder from Him of His blessings and an alert to the place of thanks. As for the testing, it is by creation together with soundness of the natural disposition and soundness of reason free from affliction, as He said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So We made him hearing and seeing﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So We made him one who has hearing by which he hears, and one who has sight by which he sees, as a favour from God upon His servants by this, a mercy from Him toward them, and a proof of His against them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 76, verse 3–4:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way, either grateful or ungrateful﴾ (3) ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles and a blazing Fire﴾ (4)

.

His saying, exalted is His praise, ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way﴾ means: Indeed, We made clear to him the path to Paradise and made known to him its way, whether he gives thanks or disbelieves. When the statement is directed to this meaning, "immā" (either) and "immā" (or) carry the sense of a conditional, and it is also permissible that "immā ... immā" have the same meaning, as in His saying: ﴿Either He punishes them or He turns to them in forgiveness﴾. Then His saying, ﴿either grateful or ungrateful﴾, is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun in "hadaynāhu" (We guided him), so the meaning of the statement, when it is directed to this interpretation, is: Indeed, We guided him to the way, either wretched or happy. Some grammarians of Basra used to say this, as in His saying: ﴿the punishment or the Hour﴾, as if you had not mentioned "immā"; he said: and if you wish, you begin with what follows it and put it in the nominative.

Those who interpret the Qur'an hold views similar to what we have said on this matter.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, We have prepared for those who disbelieve in Our blessings and oppose Our command chains by which they are securely bound, firmly fastened in the Hellfire, ﴿and shackles﴾, meaning: and their hands will be fastened with shackles to their necks within it.

* *

His saying: ﴿and a blazing Fire﴾

He says: and a fire kindled against them, blazing intensely.

His saying, exalted is His praise, ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way﴾ means: Indeed, We made clear to him the path to Paradise and made known to him its way, whether he gives thanks or disbelieves. ﴿Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor.﴾

.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 76, verse 6:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿A spring from which the servants of God drink; they make it gush forth in abundance﴾

Its meaning: Indeed, those who were dutiful (abarra) by obeying their Lord in performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, they drink from a cup, which is any vessel that contains drink. ﴿Its mixture is camphor﴾ means: the mixture of the drink within it is camphor, ﴿kafuran﴾ meaning: in the fragrance of its scent, like camphor. It has been said that kafur is the name of a spring of water in Paradise. Whoever says this makes the accusative of "ʿaynan" (a spring) a substitution (radd) for "kafur," as an explanation (tabyin) of it. And whoever makes kafur a description of the drink puts "ʿaynan," meaning the spring, in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), and makes the predicate of kana the saying "kafuran." The accusative of "ʿaynan" may also be permitted from a third aspect, which is to make it accusative by the governing of "yashrabuna fiha," so that the meaning of the statement is: the righteous drink from a spring from which the servants of God drink, from a cup whose mixture is camphor. It may also be permitted to make it accusative as a praise (madh). However, the majority of the interpreters said that kafur is a description of the drink, as I have mentioned.

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed the righteous drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor﴾, he said: a people for whom it is mixed with camphor and sealed with musk.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿a spring from which the servants of God drink﴾

They drank with the water of the sea, then were mixed (taraqqaʿat)
with green seas, for them is a roaring (naʾij)

He, the Exalted, says: These righteous ones used to give food in spite of their love for it and their desire for it.

He, may His praise be exalted, by His words "needy" means: those in need whom need has humbled; ﴿and orphan﴾, who is the child whose father has died and has nothing; ﴿and captive﴾: he is the non-Muslim from the people of the abode of war who is seized by force through domination, or from the people of the qiblah who is taken and imprisoned rightfully. Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Asim related to us, who said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿They fulfil the vow﴾, he said: "When they vow for the right of Allah."

Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿They fulfil the vow﴾, he said: "They used to vow acts of obedience to Allah, such as prayer, zakat, Hajj and 'umrah, and what was obligated upon them. So Allah named them 'the righteous' by that, saying: ﴿They fulfil the vow and fear a Day whose evil will be spreading far and wide﴾."

Narrated to us Ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿They fulfil the vow﴾, he said: "By obedience to Allah, by prayer, by Hajj and by 'umrah."

Narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, regarding His words ﴿They fulfil the vow﴾, he said: "In what is not disobedience."

In the statement there is an omitted element, which is dispensed with because the context points to it, namely "kanu" (they used to). The meaning of the statement is: "Indeed the righteous drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor; they used to fulfil the vow." The word "kanu" was left out because the context indicates it. The vow (nadhr) is whatever a person makes obligatory upon himself of an act; and from it is the saying of 'Antarah:

"The two who revile my honour, and I did not revile them, and the two who vow my blood, if I do not meet them..." [Note: the phrase "la tamani'" means there is no disagreement among them that would lead some to repel what the other says. A similar usage will come in p. 126.]

And His words: ﴿and fear a Day whose evil will be spreading far and wide﴾

He, the Exalted, says: and they fear the punishment of Allah by their abandoning fulfilment of what they vowed to Allah of righteousness, on a Day whose evil was spreading far and wide, extended, long, widespread.

And with the like of what we have said in this regard, the people of ta'wil have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and fear a Day whose evil will be spreading far and wide﴾, he said: "By Allah, the evil of that Day spread until it filled the heavens and the earth. As for a man who vows that he will not maintain ties of kinship, nor give charity, nor do any good, then it is not appropriate that expiation be made for him, and that comes. From it is the saying: istatara al-sadc fi al-zujaja wa-istatal, when it extends; and this is not said of a wall." From it is the saying of al-A'sha:

"She departed, and she had left in the hearts a crack spreading far, despite her distance..." [Diwan: 165. The "mudah" is the plural of "madah"; and "madda fulanan yamduhu madhan" means he described his appearance and beauty and praised him. "Istarja'n" means they said "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return," saying it in grief over him: how he took up asceticism and abandoned the world after what he had of youth, beauty and passion!]

That is: extended, widespread.

And His words: ﴿And they give food, in spite of their love for it, to the needy﴾

He, the Exalted, says: These righteous ones used to give food in spite of their love for it and their desire for it.

And with the like of what we have said in this regard, the people of ta'wil have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to us Yahya ibn Talha al-Yarbu'i, who said: Fudayl ibn Iyad related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿in spite of their love for it﴾, he said: "While they desire it."

Narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, who said: Abu al-Iryan related to us, who said: I asked Sulayman ibn Qays Abu Muqatil ibn Sulayman regarding His words ﴿and give food, in spite of their love for it, to the needy﴾, and he said: "In spite of their love for the food."

And His words: ﴿needy﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, by His words "needy" means: those in need whom need has humbled; ﴿and orphan﴾, who is the child whose father has died and has nothing; ﴿and captive﴾: he is the non-Muslim from the people of the abode of war who is seized by force through domination, or from the people of the qiblah who is taken and imprisoned rightfully. Allah praised these righteous ones for feeding these, seeking nearness to Allah through that and seeking His good pleasure, and out of mercy toward them.

The scholars differed concerning the captive whom Allah mentioned in this place. Some of them said:

Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and give food, in spite of their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾, he said: "Allah commanded that captives be treated well, and their captives on that day were polytheists."

Narrated to us Ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿and captive﴾, he said: "Their captives on that day were polytheists, and your Muslim brother is more deserving that you feed him."

He said: Al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, from Abu 'Amr that 'Ikrimah said regarding His words ﴿and give food, in spite of their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾: he claimed that he said, "The captives in that time were polytheists."

Narrated to us Ibn Bashshar, who said: Hammad ibn Mas'adah related to us, who said: Ash'ath related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿the orphan and the captive﴾, he said: "Their captives were none but polytheists."

Others said: What is meant is: the imprisoned person from the people of the qiblah.

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to us Ibn Bashshar, who said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, who said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The captive: the imprisoned."

Narrated to me Abu Shayba ibn Abi Shayba, who said: Umar ibn Hafs related to us, who said: my father related to me, from Hajjaj, who said: Amr ibn Murrah related to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words ﴿needy, orphan, and captive﴾, "from the people of the qiblah and others." Likewise, the captive is intended to include the captives of polytheists and Muslims on that day and after it until the Hour is established.

And His words: ﴿Indeed we feed you only for the sake of Allah﴾

He, the Exalted, says: They say: "We feed you only" when they feed them, "for the sake of Allah," meaning seeking the good pleasure of Allah and nearness to Him; ﴿we desire from you no reward nor thanks﴾. They say to those whom they feed that food: "We desire from you, O people, for feeding you, no recompense and no thanks."

Regarding His words ﴿nor thanks﴾ there are two aspects of meaning: One is that it is the plural of "shukr" (thanks), just as "fulus" is the plural of "fals" and "kufur" is the plural of "kufr." The other is that it is a single verbal noun (masdar) with the sense of a plural, as one says: "qa'ada qu'udan" (he sat, sitting) and "kharaja khurujan" (he went out, going out).

And Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Salim, from Mujahid regarding ﴿We feed you only for the sake of Allah; we desire from you no reward nor thanks﴾, he said: "As for them, they did not say it, but Allah knew it from their hearts, so He praised them for it, that one who desires may be encouraged to do the same."

Narrated to us Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz, who said: Musa ibn Isma'il related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Abi al-Wadah related to us, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding ﴿We feed you only for the sake of Allah; we desire from you no reward nor thanks﴾, he said: "By Allah, they did not say it with their tongues, but Allah knew it from their hearts, so He praised them for it, that one who desires may be encouraged."

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day austere and distressing﴾ [76:10] ﴿So Allah protected them from the evil of that Day and gave them radiance and happiness﴾ [76:11].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, informing about these people whose description He has given, that they say to those whom they feed from among the needy and destitute: ﴿We feed you only for the countenance of Allah. The day has become intense (iqmatarra), yak-matirru, iqmitrar, and that is the most intense and longest of days in trial and hardship. From it is the saying of one of them:

"Sons of our paternal uncles, do you remember our trial upon you, when there was a day of qamatir?"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 76, verses 12–13:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And He will reward them for their patience with a garden and silk.﴾ ﴿Reclining therein on couches, they will see there neither sun nor bitter cold.﴾

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Reclining therein on couches﴾

He says: reclining in the Garden on thrones within canopied enclosures (hijal). These are the arai'k (ara'ik), singular arikah (arika). We have already explained this with its evidences and what the interpreters have said about it earlier, in a manner that suffices without repeating it, except that we mention at this place some of the narration that we did not mention before, if Allah the Exalted wills.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Reclining therein on couches﴾, he meant: the hijal.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Reclining therein on couches﴾, he said: We used to be told that they are the hijal, in which are beds.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Husayn, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Reclining therein on couches﴾, he said: thrones within canopied enclosures. And ﴿reclining﴾ is in the accusative here as a circumstantial state (hal) of the pronoun in "therein" (ha' and mim).

* *

And His saying: ﴿they will see there neither sun nor bitter cold﴾

He, the Exalted, says: they will not see therein a sun that would harm them with its heat, nor zamharir, which is intense cold, that would harm them with its cold.

The interpreters have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said this:

Ziyad ibn Abdullah al-Hasani narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Sa'ir narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: The zamharir: the severe cold.

The passage in full:

Wait — I must not alter. Here is the faithful translation:

"Dāniyah" is feminine because "ẓilāl" (shades) is a plural. It is mentioned that in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is masculine: ﴿and dāniyan ʿalayhim ẓilāluhā﴾, and it is masculine because the verb is placed first. In the reading that has reached me, it is ﴿wa-dānin﴾, nominative, as a resumption.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and its clusters were made easy, with ease﴾

Those who interpret have said in accordance with what we have said. Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver and cups that were glass﴾: he said: vessels of silver, and their clearness and preparation are like the clearness of glass.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 76, verse 21:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Upon them will be garments of fine green silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink to drink﴾ (76:21)

[Note: the passage is a single continuous commentary; see translation below.]

His, may He be exalted and remembered, words mean: above them, i.e., above these righteous ones, will be garments of sundus (fine silk). Some of the interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) explained His words ﴿ʿāliyahum﴾ ("upon them") as meaning: above the canopies (ḥijāl) fixed upon them, ﴿garments of sundus﴾. This view is not to be rejected, for if it refers to being above the canopies in which they are, then it has exalted them, so it is "upon them."

The readers (ahl al-qira'a) differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of Madina and Kufa, and some of the readers of Makka, read ﴿ʿāliyahum﴾ with the yā' vowelless (ʿāliyhum). ʿĀṣim, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read it with the yā' vowelled with a fatḥa (ʿāliyahum). Whoever vowels it with fatḥa makes His words ﴿ʿāliyahum﴾ a noun in the nominative agreeing with the garments, like the speaker's saying: "their outer garments are garments of sundus."

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that these are two well-known readings, close in meaning, so whichever one the reciter reads is correct.

* *

His words: ﴿garments of sundus﴾

That is: garments of fine, good dībāj (brocade silk). Sundus is what is thin of dībāj.

* *

His words: ﴿green﴾

The readers differed in reading this. Abū Jaʿfar al-Qāriʾ and Abū ʿAmr read ﴿khuḍrun﴾ with a raised (ḍamma) vowel, making it an adjective of the garments, and read ﴿istabraqin﴾ with a lowered (kasra) vowel, conjoined to sundus, meaning: and garments of istabraq. ʿĀṣim and Ibn Kathīr read ﴿khuḍrin﴾ with a lowered vowel and ﴿wa-istabraqun﴾ with a raised vowel, conjoining istabraq to the garments, meaning: upon them is istabraq, and making the "green" an adjective of the sundus. Nāfiʿ read ﴿khuḍrun﴾ with a raised vowel as an adjective of the garments and ﴿wa-istabraqun﴾ with a raised vowel conjoined to the garments. The majority of the readers of Kufa read ﴿khuḍrin wa-istabraqin﴾ both with a lowered vowel. Ibn Muḥayṣin read istabraq without declension, with a fatḥa: ﴿wa-istabraqa﴾, meaning: and garments of istabraq, and he vowelled it with fatḥa because he directed it to being a non-Arabic (aʿjamī) noun. For all these readings which we have mentioned there is a meaning and a line of reasoning other than what preceded our mention of Ibn Muḥayṣin's, but they are remote from the known usage of the Arabs, since istabraq is an indefinite noun (nakira), and the Arabs decline indefinite nouns even if they are non-Arabic. Istabraq is what is thick of dībāj. We have already mentioned the opinions of the interpreters on this earlier, so that suffices and need not be repeated here.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatada, he said: Istabraq: thick dībāj.

* *

His words: ﴿and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾

He says: their Lord will adorn them with bracelets, which are the plural of aswira (bracelet) made of silver.

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: their Lord gave these righteous ones a pure drink to drink; and among its purity is that it does not become impure urine, but rather becomes a sweat exuding from their bodies like the sweat of musk.

It was said to him: Who is this? He said: Jibrīl. It was said: And who is with you? He said: Muḥammad. They said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. They said: May God welcome him as a brother and a successor; how excellent the brother and how excellent the successor, and how excellent the arrival that has arrived. He said: So he entered, and behold, there was a man with white hair seated on a chair at the gate of Paradise, and with him were people sitting with bright faces like sheets of paper, and people in whose colours there was something. Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and do not obey from among them a sinner or ungrateful one﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning the enemy of Allah, Abu Jahl.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, that it reached him that Abu Jahl said: "If I see Muhammad praying, I will surely step on his neck." So Allah revealed: ﴿and do not obey from among them a sinner or ungrateful one﴾.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and do not obey from among them a sinner or ungrateful one﴾: "The sinner (āthim) is the guilty wrongdoer, and the ungrateful one (kafūr), all of this is one."

It was said: in ﴿aw kafūran﴾ the meaning is: "nor an ungrateful one." Al-Farra' said: "Aw" here has the function of "wa" (and), and in negation, interrogation, and conditional constructions it carries the meaning of "lā" (not). So this is from that with negation, and from it is the poet's saying:

Neither the grief of a bereaved mother is like what she felt, nor the grief of a calf whose mother the wolf (rubaʿ) has led astray,

Or the grief of an old man who lost his she-camel, on the day the pilgrims gathered and dispersed.

He meant: "nor the grief of an old man." He said: In Arabic it may also be said: "Do not obey from among them one who sins or disbelieves," so that "aw" carries a meaning close to "wa," as when you say to a man: "I will surely give you whether you ask or remain silent," meaning: "I will surely give you in every case."

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And mention the name of your Lord morning and evening﴾ (25)

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 76, verses 26–27:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And of the night, prostrate yourself to Him, and glorify Him through a long night (26). Indeed, these love the immediate (world) and leave behind them a heavy Day (27).﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And remember﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿the name of your Lord﴾, so call upon Him by it in the morning (bukrah) in the dawn prayer, and in the evening (ashiyy) in the noon and afternoon prayers. ﴿And of the night, prostrate yourself to Him﴾ means: and of the night, prostrate yourself to Him in your prayer. ﴿Glorify Him through a long night﴾ means: most of the night, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿Stand (for prayer) through the night, except a little, half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it﴾.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And of the night, prostrate yourself to Him and glorify Him through a long night﴾, that it means: the prayer and the glorification.

Then he said: This was abrogated for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and for the people, and He made it a supererogatory prayer, saying: ﴿And from the night, pray the tahajjud with it as an additional (prayer) for you﴾. He said: So He made it a supererogatory prayer.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, these love the immediate (world)﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, these polytheists who associate others with Allah love the immediate (world), meaning the worldly life; that is, they love to remain in it, and its adornment pleases them. ﴿And leave behind them a heavy Day﴾ means: and they leave behind them, neglecting, work for the Hereafter, which would have been their salvation from the punishment of Allah on that Day. Some have interpreted it to mean: "and they leave before them a heavy Day," and that is not a rejected statement; however, what we have said is more fitting to the meaning of the word.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿And leave behind them a heavy Day﴾, that he said: "The Hereafter."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We created them and strengthened their makeup. And when We will, We can replace them with others like them, a complete replacement.﴾ (28) ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way.﴾ (29)

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, who said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿We created them and strengthened their makeup﴾, he said: "We strengthened their creation."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, who said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And strengthened their makeup﴾, he said: "Their creation."

Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And strengthened their makeup﴾: "Their creation."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, the like of it.

Others said: al-Asr means the joints.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, I heard him (meaning Khallad) say: I heard Abu Sa'id, who had recited the Qur'an to Abu Hurayra, say: "I did not recite the Qur'an except to Abu Hurayra; he taught me it." Others said: rather, it is strength.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And strengthened their makeup﴾, he said: "The asr is strength."

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is the one we have chosen, because al-asr is what I have mentioned among the Arabs; and from it is the saying of al-Akhtal:

From every shunned one whose asr is strong, / easy in leading, you think him arrogant.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder﴾

It means: Indeed, this surah is a reminder for whoever takes heed, is admonished, and considers.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said.

His saying: ﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾

It means: So whoever wills, O people, takes a path to the pleasure of his Lord by acting in His obedience and desisting at His command and prohibition.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 76, verse 30–31:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ (30) ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy; but for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment.﴾ (31)

Say (the Exalted, may His remembrance be honored): ﴿And you will not will﴾ to take the path to your Lord, O people, ﴿except that Allah wills﴾ it for you, because the matter belongs to Him, not to you. In the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), it is reported, it reads: ﴿And you will not will except what Allah wills﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾

So none of you will escape what has preceded in His knowledge concerning your arrangements.

* *

And His saying: ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy﴾

He says: your Lord admits whom He wills of you into His mercy, so He accepts his repentance until he dies repentant of his error, and so He forgives him his sins and admits him into His Paradise. ﴿But for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment﴾: He says, those who wronged themselves and died in their polytheism, for them He has prepared in the Hereafter a painful, agonizing punishment, which is the punishment of Hell. The accusative of His saying ﴿the wrongdoers﴾ is because the waw is a circumstantial/object-marker governed by "a'adda" (prepared), and the meaning is: and He has prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment. It is reported that in the reading of Abdullah it reads: ﴿and for the wrongdoers He has prepared for them﴾, with the lam repeated. The Arabs may do this, and someone has recited, for one of them:

I say to her when she asks for divorce: "Why are you hastening toward my separation?"

And for another:

So they no longer ask him about what ails him: has he ascended in the path of misguided passion, or has he descended?

With the repetition of the preposition "bi" (about/with). Rather, the sentence is: they do not ask him about what is with him.

End of the commentary on Surat al-Insan.
